content.title: Guardians vs. Mariners: Prediction, Lineups, How to Watch (3/28)
content.text: The Cleveland Guardians (1–1) and the Seattle Mariners (1–1) continue their four-game series tonight at T-Mobile Park. The series is even after Seattle responded with a 5–1 win on Friday, bouncing back from Cleveland’s 6–4 Opening Day victory. The Mariners leaned on a strong outing from George Kirby, who allowed just one run on two hits over six innings while striking out six, settling in after an early home run by rookie Chase DeLauter, who has hit the long ball in each of his first two regular-season games. Seattle’s offense came almost entirely via the long ball. Two of their three hits were home runs. Cole Young delivered a three-run homer in the fourth inning and Luke Raley added a two-run shot later as insurance. Cleveland’s Gavin Williams struggled with command, walking six in five innings, while striking out seven. Saturday’s matchup features Joey Cantillo for Cleveland against Bryan Woo for Seattle. Cantillo comes off a strong first full year in the majors, finishing with a 5-3 record and 3.21 ERA over 34 appearances. He began the season in the bullpen, but became an indispensable part of their rotation in the second half, and posted a 2-0 record and 1.55 ERA in September as part of the Guardians’ historic fall run. Woo looks to sustain the momentum from an All-Star 2025 season, finishing with a 15-7 record and 2.94 ERA, striking out 198 in 186.2 innings. Expect a low-scoring affair tonight with two dominant pitchers on the mound. The Mariners have the slight edge here at home.
